issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex omits the `i` flag while HAS_KEYWORD includes it, breaking contract symmetry for case-insensitive keyframe selectors
issues.detail: PERCENTAGE_SELECTORS contains tokens like `from`/`to` which CSS treats case-insensitively. HAS_KEYWORD uses `i`; HAS_PERCENTAGE does not. The walk-filter contract should be: 'admit any rule that *might* contain a violating token.' Asymmetric casing strengthens the precondition for one branch and silently drops legitimate rules like `FROM { ... }` when primary is `keyword`. State the contract; apply it uniformly.

issues.description: Pre-filter regexes encode a weaker postcondition than the parser, risking false negatives on edge cases (comments, escapes, custom properties)
issues.detail: The walk-filter is now part of each rule's contract: 'if the regex rejects, the rule guarantees no violation exists.' But `\burl\(` matches inside comments; `\b(?:100|200|...)\b` matches inside `var(--font-700)`; `:not(` matches in attribute selectors like `[data-x=":not("]`. The fast-path postcondition must imply the slow-path postcondition. Add a brief spec comment per regex documenting the over-approximation guarantee.

issues.description: `selectorRegex = /./` sentinel leaks implementation detail into the walk contract for `percentage-unless-within-keyword-only-block`
issues.detail: Using a match-anything regex as a 'pass-through' is an abstraction leak — the caller now must know that walkRules treats `/./` as 'no filter'. Cleaner: branch on whether a filter exists and call `walkRules(cb)` vs `walkRules(regex, cb)`. The module boundary should expose intent (filter-or-not), not a regex hack.

issues.description: Repeated fast-path pattern across six rules has no shared abstraction or named contract
issues.detail: Each rule reinvents the same idiom: 'compile a presence regex, bail early if absent.' This is an emerging ADT — call it `quickReject(value, primary)` or document the convention in a comment. Without naming it, future contributors will not know whether the fast-path must over-approximate (safe) or may under-approximate (unsafe). SPEC-MISSING for a pattern that now spans the codebase.

issues.description: import-notation `url` branch inverts the filter polarity vs the others, which is correct but undocumented and easy to break
issues.detail: For `primary === 'url'`, the code returns when `url(` IS present — the opposite condition from sibling rules. This is right (violation = string-form when url expected), but the asymmetry deserves a one-line spec comment stating the precondition each branch is filtering for. Otherwise a future maintainer will 'fix' the apparent inconsistency.

review.summary: The PR is a sound performance optimization that pushes cheap presence checks ahead of expensive parsing — a legitimate abstract pattern. The abstract data type emerging here is "fast-reject filter that must over-approximate the slow-path matcher." That contract is implicit and unspecified across six rules. The HAS_PERCENTAGE / HAS_KEYWORD case-flag asymmetry is a concrete LSP-style violation of that contract. Recommend naming the pattern, documenting the over-approximation invariant, and fixing the case-insensitivity asymmetry before merge.
